summary: Delivered I21a: real shared combat/Stack model, typed reducers/codec/relevant replay tuples, mandatory record-boundary cleanup, source-bound invocation lowering, and reusable production Compose combat/Stack/action/contents components. Eleven shared-core tests, nine native-controller host tests and five native presentation/context tests pass; affected existing gameplay/setup tests and incremental debug APK build pass. This is not an integrated normal-table journey: I21b retains real server/session admission/execution, I13 movement/Stack guard compatibility, I19 token/link adapters, I15/I16 Canvas/gesture/action wiring, I20 relative advance-then-close and retained history/recovery integration. Parent I21 and B5 remain unfinished; no device, database/schema, UI-documentation, release or independent-review claim.
selectionReason: Supervisor leased useful speculative I21 development at the exact supplied clean base and dependency commit. Its shared reducer and reusable native components can be delivered without editing pending I13/I14/I16/I19 lanes, integration checkout or authoritative state. Acceptance must still honor latest prerequisites and sole-supervisor lease/model/session checks.
executedAssertions: CombatAndStackTest: 11 shared tests cover codec/individual deterministic replay, one combat occurrence per source across roles, paired membership and local insertion, blocker conversion/append/reuse, empty-pair cleanup, explicit closure/captured-area safety, occurrence-link cleanup, unlimited independent effects, source read-through, semantic Stack entry/source-ID guard and play scope, stale admission/removal/reorder guards, frozen read-only reorder/removal, and exact relevant cleanup/placement tuples.

Source-departure and token-freeze tests exercise the production GameplayRules.record hook with explicit candidate boards, not actual I13/I19 movement/removal commands. They retain blocker-only pairs and independent live effects across locations, capture exact last-live token fields before resets/deletion, and reject non-token disappearance. Those hook tests are not end-to-end movement/token/recovery coverage.

CombatStackControllerTest: 9 host tests cover command dispatch/replay through the actual shared reducer, individual area/declaration/tap nodes, no forced untap/no-op fabrication, bound-source alias normalization, individual occurrence removal, predicted Stack predecessor guards, spatial and blockers-first row ordering, uniform destination/role, subset insertion and no-op prefix anchors, whole-drop preflight, stale-prefix rejection without substitution, frozen-source skipping and quick/full-path separation.

CombatStackPresentationTest: 5 host tests cover compact wider-side pair widths, common card scale/rotated envelopes, both-side before/between/after insertion destinations, closed versus empty open combat, three visible Stack entries with all 27 retained ordered identities/count, explicit selected-face contextual destinations, ambiguous/missing metadata manual fallback, and live-source versus frozen read-only action/covered-label behavior.

Existing GameplayTest and PlayTest pass after shared model/record changes. Incremental protocol/Android compilation and assembleDebug pass. A final retained-menu Close binding correction remembers the original area ID and disables the control if sync replaces it; the final incremental APK compiles that change, while actual Compose interaction remains an I21b native assertion. apk-final.json identifies the final artifact; boundary.json retains the earlier intermediate APK and state-byte check. Exact JUnit XML is retained losslessly in run-owned JSON; failed compile/row-order diagnostics are also retained. No clean build, full suite, device lifecycle or UI-documentation edit was run.

deferredAssertions.assertions: Independent complete manual-toolkit journey/review, native device/server/history/recovery assertions and final affected full-suite, compatibility and complete mock/interface/orientation gates remain required. Requirement/feedback IDs below are traceability only, not executed acceptance coverage or release-gate changes.

integrationSeams: BoardState.combat stores paired sides/occurrence IDs; stackEffects stores independent source references. The existing STACK PlayContainer.cards is the single top-first mixed real-card/effect-ID order. I13 must use CombatStackRules.identities/stackDigest for BOTH real-card additions and effect additions, preserving D-247 domain-separated ordered kind/ID/source/play comparison. Do not merge the old real-card-only digest unchanged or add source/field/board locks.

GameplayRules.record closes source/occurrence invariants before producing one mutation. I13/I19 must feed their candidate board through this boundary and retain their own precise movement/removal/reset tuples. Token freeze reads the pre-transition PlayCard, including owner/face/cover/orientation/corner/counters/note/placement, not a reset candidate or creation snapshot. Frozen effects are never editable/cloneable sources or replacement cards. Existing non-token sources stay live after moves/resets.

ProjectionLink is the narrow D-120 projection-to-projection relationship with same-transition cleanup. It is NOT the source relationship, selection or a replacement for I19 generic card/player links. Integrate the common endpoint registry without duplicate relationship storage; preserve surviving effect links and remove only links whose actual endpoints disappear. Generic source-token links still belong to I19 cleanup.

CombatStackController binds view/source identities at menu capture, normalizes live-source aliases once, and returns original ordered GameCommands plus provisional prediction. Its dispatch callback queues originals without acknowledgement waits; it never owns accepted state or a second local authoritative game. GameSession at this base has no gameplay queue, and server sources do not yet dispatch GameplayRules. I21b must connect the real session/transaction paths rather than claim these host plans are integrated.

Compose CombatActions/StackActions execute real shared plans via required onPlan callbacks. CombatDestinationActions/StackDestinationActions and CombatLane supply exact bound semantic destinations to the normal move/drop adapter. CombatQuickActions supplies a captured area ID to I20's actual relative advance-then-close composition; that callback is intentionally not implemented as a local turn write or fake controller method. Full standalone primitives exist, but actual Next-step/table wiring is retained I21b.

CombatStackPresentation derives dp geometry from supplied ordinary-table card dimensions, preserves tapped envelopes and source-owner borders, separates gold source relationship emphasis from selected occurrence IDs, and renders no insertion rectangles/plus signs. StackPile has one top-left circular total badge and top-plus-two drawing; StackContents retains every mixed entry in order. I15/I16 must use the same geometry for actual normal-table touch/drop/accessibility and the normal display-only card renderer/inspection policy.

GameplayHistory retains individual combat/Stack relevant tuples and isolates Stack mutations; the base grouping is only the earlier scalar/movement scaffold. Reconcile with I14's complete grouping/history processor and retain all original grouping/closure/exposure/Undo/recovery obligations before accepting I21b. No authoritative history node, branch control or shared Undo stack was created locally; returned nodes are provisional prediction only.
